[{"role": "assistant", "parts": [{"type": "text", "content": "An **agent trace** is a recorded sequence of events showing how an AI/LLM agent handled a task. It commonly includes the input and context, model requests and responses, tool calls and their results, state changes, and operational details such as timestamps, latency, token use, retries, and errors. Some systems also record intermediate plans or summaries.

Traces are useful for **debugging failures**, understanding why an agent took a particular path, measuring performance and cost, evaluating behavior, and reproducing or auditing runs. They can also help identify where a workflow stalled or a tool returned an unexpected result.

The term is **not standardized**. In one system, an “agent trace” may mean a full, ordered record of the run; in another, it may mean only a structured observability trace of requests and tool calls. It does **not necessarily include the model’s private internal reasoning**: a trace may record visible outputs or summaries without exposing hidden chain-of-thought.
